dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "17 West annual-plan renewals were posted on 31 May, worth $1,506.29 | recharges.csv; posted_at, term_days, amount_usd; n=17 | High"
"Cash and ledger totals reconcile with zero difference for both batches | dealer_import_log.csv; cash_total, ledger_total, difference | High"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Operations state that annual-plan files use the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posted date | email-dealer-reconciliation.eml | Medium"
"All 17 had May effective dates (1–28 May)"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"Pipeline defect: not supported by the supplied evidence; both May 31 dealer batches reconcile exactly and match the documented submission process."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Perform a targeted reconciliation of the 17 source event IDs against the original dealer files before making any accounting adjustment."
"The files do not establish whether any human manually triggered or altered the uploads."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue is indicated by the supplied evidence."
"Keep the May 31 batches unchanged and retain the transaction/import evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Manipulated reporting: not supported because all 17 affected renewals have effective dates in May, not after the May posting date." May effective dates make the pattern consistent with legitimate event timing, but do not by themselves rule out manipulation of retention reporting.

"Pipeline defect: not supported by the supplied evidence; both May 31 dealer batches reconcile exactly and match the documented submission process." Reconciliation and process consistency reduce concern but do not fully exclude a pipeline defect, especially one affecting downstream event-time analytics.

The high confidence in the overall judgment is somewhat stronger than warranted because the submission does not test downstream analytics or explicitly verify the two dealer identities and original-file contents beyond the stated reconciliation checks.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect, but missed the important benign-yet-material alternative that the posting-time quirk can distort downstream retention, cohort, or month-end analytics even when cash and entitlement reconciliation is correct.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly test downstream reports using effective_event_date rather than posted_at, and recommend correcting or documenting those analytics while preserving the reconciled accounting batches.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South tickets fell from 198 to 124 in equal 30-day pre/post-pilot windows"
"487 of 2,709 NovaIVR sessions ended at issue_menu; the email states sessions ending before authentication are outside CareDesk containment reporting"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "it is not yet sufficient to conclude that customer experience improved or to justify national expansion"
"We do not know whether case-creation/routing rules changed, whether RESOLVED sessions remain resolved, or what happens to subscribers who leave before authentication"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Fewer underlying service problems: not supported because South service events and estimated affected accounts increased after the pilot."

"Proven customer-experience improvement: not established because the containment metric excludes sessions ending before authentication and we have not yet verified repeat contacts after RESOLVED outcomes."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Continue the South pilot without national expansion."
"performing a targeted audit of pre-authentication sessions and 7-day repeat contacts for a sample of NovaIVR RESOLVED sessions"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What exact IVR stages and outcomes are included in the CareDesk containment calculation, and which sessions are excluded?"
"Can you provide a sample of NovaIVR sessions marked RESOLVED and their subsequent CareDesk contacts so we can compare true resolution with the dashboard result?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Fewer underlying service problems: not supported because South service events and estimated affected accounts increased after the pilot." Service-event counts and affected-account estimates are relevant counterevidence, but they do not by themselves establish that underlying customer friction or all service problems did not decline.

"A general company-wide decline in complaints: not supported because the other regions were broadly stable or increased while South declined." The regional ticket comparison weakens this explanation, but ticket counts are themselves an imperfect complaint measure and do not directly establish company-wide complaint trends.
The overall "Confidence: High" is somewhat stronger than warranted because end-to-end journey outcomes, case-creation history, and repeat contacts remain unresolved.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have genuinely reduced transfers and resolved some customer journeys, while the observed ticket decline is also amplified by a measurement failure for pre-authentication sessions. The submission handles this mixed interpretation reasonably well, but does not explicitly test whether reduced transfers represent successful self-service rather than abandonment or unrecorded contact.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quantify end-to-end outcomes by linking IVR sessions—including pre-authentication abandonments and errors—to subsequent CareDesk contacts, repeat attempts, and sampled call outcomes, stratified by terminal stage and pilot version.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv and the impact_mw field for the claim that all four rows are zero.
It cites the row count and fields for cleared=yes, severity=warning, missing values, and duplicates.
The submission does not cite timestamps or other event fields that would support a recovery or duration assessment.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It identifies two plausible interpretations of zero impact: genuine zero impact versus a default or unpopulated field.
It proposes comparing the export with underlying telemetry, which is a relevant cross-check.
Its rejection of duplicate-event corruption relies mainly on '0 duplicate rows' and unique inverter IDs, which does not exclude non-identical duplicate or repeated events.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion is appropriately scoped: 'Do not escalate equipment failure from this file alone.'
It explicitly conditions stopping on confirmation that zero impacts are genuine measurements.

It does not discuss the known limitation that a seven-minute communications warning with zero MW impact and quick recovery is not evidence of equipment failure, nor does it prioritize the most decision-changing check precisely.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: 'Perform one cheap check of how impact_mw is populated or compare these events with underlying telemetry' is proportionate and operationally sensible.
The proposed check can distinguish a real zero-impact event from an export or field-population problem.
The action is somewhat broad and does not specify comparing event intervals with MW telemetry, communications status, or recovery timing.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion not to escalate equipment failure is consistent with four zero-MW records, cleared events, and the absence of evidence of material production impact.
The conditional stop recommendation is consistent with the limited evidence and avoids inventing a plant problem from a communications warning.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'Duplicate-event corruption is rejected' is too strong: zero exact duplicate rows and unique inverter IDs rule out only a narrow form of duplication, not repeated or malformed events with differing fields.

The statement that there are 'no missing values' is treated as observed from the CSV, but the submission does not identify whether this was checked across all relevant fields or only selected columns.
The claim that the export is 'very small' is an observation, but its significance remains speculative because completeness expectations are unknown.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The zero impacts may be genuine: the events could be short communications warnings that cleared without any MW loss. The remaining alternative worth testing is that impact_mw is defaulted or not populated correctly; the file alone cannot distinguish these.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the cheap validation discriminating and timestamp-specific: verify how impact_mw is derived, then compare each event interval with independent MW telemetry and communications/recovery records. This would test both the suspected export defect and the benign zero-impact interpretation.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv, the dsm_penalty_rs field, and 96 blocks per day for the arithmetic reproduction.
It also cites AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md and dispatch_blocks.csv for the matching commercial totals and schedule-generation figures.
It does not identify the relevant base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw fields or explicitly show the 29 May same-day comparison.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly notes that the comparison is “one conventional day versus one AI-assisted day, with differing operating conditions.”
It tests the arithmetic-error explanation using an independent block-level recalculation.

It does not test or construct the same-day counterfactual using 29 May base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw, and its weather/day-specific explanation is acknowledged rather than investigated with another evidence channel.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The statement that “the evidence does not establish that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction” is appropriately calibrated.
The recommendation distinguishes the observed before-vs-after difference from a causal effect and identifies the need for multiple comparable observations.
It does not prioritize the immediate decision-changing same-day counterfactual before proposing future matched or randomized periods.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot for controlled evaluation, but do not treat 31.6% as a causal effect or expand it nationally yet” is a sensible, proportionate action.
The proposed collection of matched or randomized pilot/control periods is directionally useful.
The next test is less discriminating than it could be because it omits the available 29 May base-versus-submitted schedule comparison.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that 31.6% is reproducible as an observed day-over-day difference but not established as causal matches the evidence and the different-day comparison.
The submission avoids the opposite error of asserting a controlled 31.6% causal estimate.
It does not clearly preserve or quantify the smaller same-day pilot benefit required by comparing base_schedule_mw with submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the schedule-generation gap “falls from 1,515.97 MWh to 1,131.05 MWh” is not sufficiently traceable as a same-day counterfactual because the submission does not identify which value is base_schedule_mw and which is submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May.

The phrase “the narrower supported claim” is incomplete: the day-over-day 31.6% reduction is observed, but the submission should also report the separately supported same-day difference rather than leaving the impression that only a cross-day comparison is available.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot day performed better than the prior conventional day, but much of that difference may reflect weather, operating conditions, or other day-specific factors. A same-day comparison of 29 May base_schedule_mw against submitted_schedule_mw can support a smaller operational benefit without establishing that the full 31.6% day-over-day reduction was caused by the pilot.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly calculate and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw, then distinguish that smaller pilot-day benefit from the uncontrolled 28-to-29 May comparison.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "A likely declaration-entry error is not supported because the declared 90211000 agrees with the Swiss tariff reference for the same product and date."
"The mismatch is better explained by comparing a Swiss local tariff code with the Helios commodity code."
"The applicable Swiss Tares classification or product-specific customs ruling for P1001 effective on 2025-11-04 could materially change the judgment."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do not escalate CH-2025-000522 as a likely declaration error."
"The applicable Swiss Tares classification or product-specific customs ruling for P1001 effective on 2025-11-04 could materially change the judgment."
"First verify the applicable Swiss Tares/ruling classification"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The mismatch appears to be a code-system/reference-data issue"
"The schema does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates, or ruling authority."
"Update the control to compare the same country-specific code system and effective-date version."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not amend the declaration automatically."
"First verify the applicable Swiss Tares/ruling classification"
"Do not escalate CH-2025-000522 as a likely declaration error."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The product identity is also consistent across the declaration and invoice." The submission does not provide an exact invoice file location, row, or passage supporting this claim.

"The mismatch appears to be a code-system/reference-data issue" is well supported as the leading explanation, but the cited evidence does not by itself establish that 90211000 is the legally applicable Swiss classification; the submission appropriately qualifies this with the missing Tares/ruling evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The declaration could still contain a classification error if the applicable Swiss Tares entry or a product-specific customs ruling effective on 2025-11-04 maps P1001 to 90211090 or another code. Agreement with the Swiss tariff matrix is not conclusive if that matrix is not the controlling source.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide exact, independently verifiable invoice and reference-matrix rows plus the applicable Swiss Tares or ruling result for P1001 on 2025-11-04, explicitly identifying each code system, nomenclature version, effective date, and authority.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Preference = Yes for P1006 on 2025-09-18 | declaration.pdf | High"
"SUP-02/P1006 record expired on 2025-07-31 | supplier_origin_register.csv | High"
"No current register document found for SUP-02/P1006 on 2025-09-18 | supplier_declaration_reference.txt | High"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "No register match means the preference claim is definitely false" is rejected because the register may not always be updated and documents may exist in category folders.
"US manufacturing country proves or disproves preference" is also rejected because the workshop notes state that manufacturing-country data was not designed to prove preference.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preference claim is not currently supported by the available evidence, but it is not disproved."
"The search note states that this does not prove that no document exists outside the register."
"The actual supplier declaration for SUP-02/P1006, its validity on 2025-09-18, and the specific preference-origin rule used for the claim are missing."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "the register may not always be updated and documents may exist in category folders"
"Supplier declarations may exist outside the register"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "hold the preference claim pending verification rather than automatically amending or rejecting it."
"Do not automatically amend or disclose until the evidence is verified."
"Verify the supplier, product, document validity, and applicable origin rule."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The confidence rating of "High" for "No current register document found" is stronger than the described search evidence warrants; it establishes a search result, not the nonexistence of a valid declaration outside the register.

The submission says the supplier register record "expired on 2025-07-31" but provides no row, field, or quotation beyond the filename, so the underlying expiry value is not independently traceable within the submission.
The source-support assertions are plausible, but the submission does not quote or identify the relevant passages in the cited files, limiting independent verification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: SUP-02 may have held a valid supplier declaration on 2025-09-18 that was stored outside the supplier register or was not reflected in the register; in that case, the expired register entry would not undermine the preference claim. Conversely, without the declaration and applicable preferential-origin rule, the claim remains unverified rather than established.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and quote the actual SUP-02/P1006 supplier declaration and applicable preferential-origin rule, including validity dates and product scope, while documenting the register search path and its limitations.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "181 of 215 released rows have qcore_release_ts exactly at 02:10:00" — specific field, count, and value are identified.
"The SOP target is 24 hours from required evidence available to disposition" and "LabTrack is a 48h analytics extract" — relevant SOP and freshness evidence are cited.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "This pattern suggests the field may represent a reporting/batch timestamp rather than the actual disposition time" — separates a timestamp mechanism from the apparent cycle-time symptom.
"I would not reject the possibility that the process genuinely takes about 1.5 days" — preserves a viable operational-delay explanation rather than asserting the artifact is the sole cause.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The operational claim is plausible. However, this does not validate the KPI definition or timestamp quality" — confidence is differentiated by claim.
"I also would not treat every >24-hour lab-to-release interval as a confirmed SLA breach" — appropriately limits conclusions because the SOP start event is missing.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not build the dashboard KPI yet" — appropriately reframes the task from KPI construction to validity checking.
"Verify qcore_release_ts semantics and reconstruct a small sample using required-evidence-available to authorized disposition time" — proposes a small, reversible validation step aligned to the SOP.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "I would not reject the possibility that the process genuinely takes about 1.5 days" — identifies the strongest competing explanation.
The submission distinguishes that possibility from KPI validity, but does not yet test the genuine-delay explanation against independent event or authorization timestamps.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The key missing evidence is the data-catalog definition of qcore_release_ts and a small sample of actual QCore authorization timestamps" — requests focused, high-value evidence.
"If qcore_release_ts is a true disposition timestamp... If it is a snapshot/batch timestamp..." — explicitly connects the evidence to the decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The inference that qcore_release_ts may be a reporting or batch timestamp is plausible, but the shared snapshot-time coincidence and concentration at 02:10 do not establish that mechanism without QCore metadata or event records.

The submission notes LabTrack freshness but does not establish that QCore and LabTrack are from a coherent point-in-time snapshot, so any reconstructed cross-source sample remains temporally qualified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The process may genuinely have approximately 39 hours of receipt-to-release elapsed time, while the apparent SLA issue remains unresolved because the SOP clock starts at required-evidence availability and the release timestamp semantics are uncertain.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly verify source_freshness for both QCore and LabTrack and align the extracts before joining them to event or authorization records; this would test both timestamp semantics and temporal consistency rather than only the field definition.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "24 open requests have $166,495.60 apparent quote value"; "MaintStar-global snapshot is 2026-06-26 and refreshes monthly"; "Reservations and qualification restrictions affect transfers" — cites relevant source files and distinguishes the main evidence channels, but does not provide row IDs, field values, or an auditable calculation for the 39.7% candidate-value figure.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "semantic-search pilot, but the search should produce candidates, not automatic transfer decisions"; "Similar descriptions mean the parts are interchangeable is rejected because manufacturer identity, revision, UOM and qualification must also be checked" — separates retrieval from transferability and tests exact-MPN, revision, reservation, and quantity issues. It does not fully trace how stale, asynchronous extracts affect each individual match.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "0% actionable now because the global stock snapshot is stale"; "Approximately 39.7% of the value has a plausible cross-site candidate and needs engineering/current-stock checks" — recognizes source freshness and separates candidate from actionable value. However, the 0% actionable conclusion is stronger than the evidence supports: staleness reduces confidence in availability but does not itself establish that every otherwise compliant candidate is non-actionable.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "the search should produce candidates, not automatic transfer decisions"; "Refresh current stock/reservation data, then obtain receiving-engineer confirmation" — provides a safe reframing and avoids automated transfers. It would be more useful with a small prioritized pilot, explicit success criteria, and a request-level calculation of candidate versus actionable savings.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Similar descriptions mean the parts are interchangeable is rejected"; "The whole $166,495.60 is avoidable is rejected"; "Exact MPN matches can be transferred immediately is also rejected" — addresses several plausible but unsafe interpretations and gives evidence-based reasons. It does not identify a stronger competing explanation for the apparent opportunity, such as temporal inconsistency producing misleading stock joins, or specify the observation that would revive it.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Refresh current stock/reservation data"; "obtain receiving-engineer confirmation"; "Confirm site qualification"; "investigate negative availability quantities" — requests relevant, decision-changing evidence and explains that results could move value into or out of actionable savings. The requests are not prioritized by expected value and do not identify the smallest discriminating query or the highest-value requests to test first.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "I would call 0% actionable now because the global stock snapshot is stale" overstates what staleness establishes; it supports downgrading availability confidence, not necessarily zero actionable value.

"Approximately 39.7% of the value has a plausible cross-site candidate" is not accompanied by a request-level value reconciliation or calculation, so the percentage is not auditable from the submission.

The candidate rows label several items as having "same MPN/revision/UOM, free stock" but do not show the separate qualification, reservation, criticality, and currentness checks needed to support transferability.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence supports semantic search as a candidate-generation tool, but stale global data may make only the availability component uncertain rather than making all candidates non-actionable. Some exact-MPN, matching-revision, unrestricted candidates could become actionable after a targeted current-stock and reservation check; conversely, asynchronous extracts could also invalidate more of the apparent 39.7% opportunity than currently shown.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Create an auditable top-value request-to-stock reconciliation using a current, timestamped stock and reservation extract, with manufacturer part number, revision/configuration, UOM, qualification, reservation/criticality, and site fields shown for each candidate. Use that reconciliation to calculate candidate value and actionable value separately before broadening the pilot.
